evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Anthropic (ANT) $1.5 Trillion IPO! Am I Buying? (2026-11-19)
evidence.claim: Khoo's 5-moat audit of Anthropic: only barriers-to-entry strong (billions in compute), but 4-5 frontier players leapfrog each other's lead every few months (Claude/GPT/Gemini); switching costs low (exports, no lock-in), pricing power unproven (price-war risk), network effect weak — moat narrow/unproven.
evidence.relation: durable-moat test failed -> can lose entire moat on one competitor leapfrog; not holdable through -30/50% drawdown

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Anthropic (ANT) $1.5 Trillion IPO! Am I Buying? (2026-11-19)
evidence.claim: Quantitative: revenue growth decelerated ~144% to 47% in most recent quarter; P/S 42x vs Nvidia 10x; reverse-DCF at 12% discount needs >Microsoft-scale revenue ($423B, +50%/yr for 5y) to justify $83; scenario-weighted fair value ~$68 -> IPO 10-22% overpriced, no margin of safety.
evidence.relation: decelerating growth + premium valuation -> negative expected return at IPO/opening price

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Anthropic (ANT) $1.5 Trillion IPO! Am I Buying? (2026-11-19)
evidence.claim: Historical post-IPO pattern Khoo cites: even great listings fell hard after IPO (Visa -53% from peak, Meta -61%, Uber -71%, Palantir -87%, SpaceX -54% and not recovered); advice: wait for >=50% off peak or ~30% below day-1 close before taking a position.
evidence.relation: first-day hype premium mean-reverts -> early entry timing risk

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Anthropic (ANT) $1.5 Trillion IPO! Am I Buying? (2026-11-19)
evidence.claim: Khoo's personal verdict: sitting this IPO out; slightly overvalued, not crazy overvalued.
